thread:
infra-oncall: Heads-up: eu-west3 NVMe scrub backlog spiked after last night's scrub-policy deploy. We're seeing attach latencies climb >5s for GPU pods and the provisioner is holding pods pending. Provision failures ~20% on recent attempts. digging...
sre-bot: ALERT: metric nvme.scrub_backlog_seconds > 600 (eu-west3) :pager:
maya: confirming. scrub backlog jumped at 02:12 UTC, aligned with the policy change that widened the scrub window. quick snapshot from affected node: 
```
$ iostat -x 1 3
Device: rrqm/s wrqm/s r/s w/s rkB/s wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm %util
nvme0n1 0.00  32.00 12.00 48.00 1024  8192  176.00    3.42   5.3   1.1    6.0   0.15  90.0
```
maya: scrub workers saturated nvme queues, iops for attach ops degraded.
shawn: can we throttle janitor scrub concurrency temporarily? that'll reduce immediate IO pressure but increases backlog/wear window. tradeoff vs provisioning failures/cost.
ashley: cost note — last week similar provisioning stalls caused ~12% spot churn and extra egress/relocation cost. short term it's cheaper to reduce scrub concurrency and accept backlog. longer term we should tighten scrub windows.
matt: i'll push a quick patch to janitor: set --scrub-max-concurrency=2 for eu-west3 and bump back after backlog drains. canary to 3 nodes first. ETA ~15m.
maya: also recommend adding a short-term scheduler tweak: lower attach timeout to 6s so failing attaches fall back sooner to another region when cross-region burst allowed.
shawn: add an alert: scrub_backlog_seconds > 300 -> page oncall and escalate to eng-infra. and a dashboard panel for attach_latency_p50/p95.
ashley: cross-region burst ok up to 10% capacity for critical GPU workloads; cost team notified. make sure we tag the traffic.
infra-oncall: matt please proceed. will monitor and post results.
matt: rolling canary now, patch applied to 3 canary nodes. logs: 
```
2024-06-XXT02:45:12Z janitor: set concurrency=2 for eu-west3
2024-06-XXT02:45:20Z provisioner: requeueing pending pods, attach latency p95 -> 2.1s
```
maya: seeing attach failures drop in canary. backlog backlog_seconds dropped from ~800 -> ~220 over 6m. good sign.
shawn: once canary looks stable, roll to fleet. also open follow-up: tighten scrub scheduling so heavy scrubs never overlap with peak provisioning windows.
infra-oncall: rolling to fleet in 10m. will follow up with post-mortem and cost delta. action items: matt deploy full roll, maya add alerts + dashboard, shawn draft scrub-schedule proposal, ashley confirm cost guardrails.
ashley: acked.
infra-oncall: closing thread once backlog < 60s and provision failures < 2% for 30m.
